about.title: Amador City Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Amador City is among the smallest incorporated towns in California, home to just 199 people, and a loss here is felt by nearly everyone. The most recent final crash year, 2025, recorded one injury collision, two people hurt, and no traffic deaths inside city limits. Even so, families in Amador County do lose loved ones to causes that reach beyond a local crash count: a collision on SR-49 or SR-88 during a drive out of town, a fall, a medical error, a workplace accident, or a defective product. When a death traces back to someone else's carelessness, California law allows a spouse, domestic partner, or children to bring a civil wrongful death claim, with certain dependents and heirs eligible in other circumstances. That claim can address funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We listen, then connect you with an independent attorney who works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Amador City Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, and children, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney you're matched with can explain where your family stands before you decide anything.

items.title: Awareness of the two-year clock
items.desc: Most California wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a public agency is involved. Connecting early keeps your options open while you grieve.

items.title: A full picture of recoverable losses
items.desc: A claim can account for funeral and burial costs, the income and support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Network attorneys handle these cases on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Amador City had no traffic deaths in 2025. Does that mean wrongful death claims don't happen here?
items.answer: Not at all. Public crash records for Amador City show one injury collision and two people injured in 2025, but wrongful death claims are not limited to local traffic. Many losses involve residents traveling on SR-88, SR-49, Fiddletown Road, or SR-16, and others stem from medical care, workplaces, or unsafe property anywhere in Amador County.

items.question: If there is already a criminal case, do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, they are separate. A criminal case is brought by the state and may lead to penalties for the person responsible, but it does not compensate your family. A wrongful death claim is a civil action your family brings to recover losses such as funeral costs, lost support, and the loss of companionship, and it can proceed whether or not charges are filed.
